scope: Fiscal impact, audits and evidence of results for India's direct-benefit and 'freebie' schemes, 2018–2026: RBI's June 2022 risk analysis and 2025-26 State Finances report, PRS State of State Finances 2025-26 (women's UCT burden by state, off-budget borrowing, subsidies), CAG Karnataka's guarantee-scheme findings and the government's rebuttal, the Supreme Court freebies reference (2022–26) and the PM's July 2022 'revdi' speech set beside BJP states' own schemes, and causal evidence on cycles, NREGS delivery and biometric exclusion. Computes base rates: share of states with women's UCTs by year, UCT share of revenue expenditure, and pre- vs post-election launch timing against a uniform null with BH correction across the whole fleet's scheme list. Deliberately leaves announcement/approval chronology, beneficiary counts and election results to the sibling files (women-cash, central, elections-timing, literature, vendors); scheme records here carry only fiscal and evidence fields and merge by id.

claims.lab: Launches cluster in the 12 months before elections — for every party
claims.d: Across 34 fleet schemes with a determinable launch and election cycle, 14 (41%) launched within 12 months before the next election vs 6.8 expected (20%) if launches were spread uniformly across each cycle (risk ratio 2.06; one-sided Monte Carlo p≈0.004, survives Benjamini–Hochberg at q=0.05 across 12 tests). narratives.strongestCounter: The list is salience-selected; the excess is identical across parties; post-poll delivery is also common; the sibling's incumbent-win split (8/8 vs 8/14) is not significant (Fisher p=0.051) and big-spending incumbents lost (YSRCP 2024, BRS 2023, TMC 2026, DMK 2026 per elections-timing.json). Timing excess ≠ vote effect.
narratives.whatWouldChangeThis: A census of all DBT launches with dates, and constituency-level variation in scheme exposure linked to vote swings.

narratives.claim: Aadhaar-based DBT eliminated leakage in welfare delivery.
narratives.strongestCase: AP Smartcards RCT: less leakage in NREGS and pensions, faster payments, no loss of access; improved NREGS implementation raised earnings 14%.
narratives.strongestCounter: Stricter biometric verification in Jharkhand PDS cut corruption but 1.5–2 million legitimate beneficiaries lost access at some point; PM-KISAN and Ladki Bahin later removed large numbers as ineligible (central.json, women-cash.json) — inclusion errors survived DBT.

symmetryCheck: Same lens, every party. (1) Fiscal weight of women's UCTs, 2025-26 BE share of revenue expenditure: JMM Jharkhand 12.1%, INC Karnataka 9.2%, TMC WB 8.9%, BJP Delhi 7.1% (budgeted), BJP MP 6.4%, Mahayuti MH 5.9%, BJP Odisha 5.1%, BJP Assam 4.3%, BJP Chhattisgarh 4.0%, DMK TN 3.7%, BJP Haryana 3.4%, INC HP 0.3%. Opposition-run states carry the heaviest single burdens (JH, KA, WB); BJP states hold the most states and 50.8% of the money. (2) RBI Jun 2022 freebies ranking: AAP, YSRCP, JMM, BJP occupy the top four; the AAP top slot is inflated by an unenacted promise, the BJP slot is a legacy power subsidy. (3) The PM's 'revdi' speech set beside BJP states' own schemes: the lens produces an adverse finding for the BJP on consistency; applied to AAP and DMK, their Supreme Court filings defend free utilities as Article 38 welfare while AAP's Punjab ₹1,000 women's promise went unenacted — also a consistency gap. (4) Audit scrutiny: CAG's strongest published language located here targets an INC state (Karnataka, 'loop of indebtedness'); comparable CAG state-finance text for BJP-run MP and Maharashtra, or TMC-run WB, was not retrieved — an asymmetry of our retrieval, not necessarily of CAG's findings (see gaps). (5) Off-budget borrowing: the largest declared stocks sit with BRS Telangana (2021-22) and Mahayuti Maharashtra (2024-25). (6) Timing: pre-poll launch rates are 47% (BJP/NDA) vs 37% (others), Fisher p=0.73. The method yields the same alarming pattern for every party, so the pattern is a property of electoral cycles, not of any one party.
